summary: NVIDIA presents an exceptionally strong fundamental profile: revenue grew 85.2% YoY in the latest quarter (E11) and annual revenue has compounded from $27.0B (2023) to $215.9B (2026) (E28), alongside best-in-class profitability (74.1% gross, 63.0% net margin, 114.3% ROE) (E13, E15, E16) and a net-cash balance sheet ($53.17B cash vs $12.81B debt) (E19, E20). Cash generation is robust with $125.65B operating cash flow TTM (E18). Despite a $5.02T market cap (E6), the forward P/E of 16.30 and PEG of 0.63 (E8, E10) look reasonable against this growth, and 59 analysts rate it strong_buy with a mean target of $298.93 vs the $207.41 price (E26, E27, E3). The main offsets are a stretched price/book of 25.70 (E9), high volatility (beta 2.20) (E24), and a complete absence of competitive/moat evidence.

dimensions.rationale: Latest-quarter revenue grew 85.2% YoY and earnings 214.5% YoY (E11, E12), and the annual revenue trend shows rapid, sustained acceleration from $27.0B (2023) to $60.9B (2024) to $130.5B (2025) to $215.9B (2026) (E28). The PEG ratio of 0.63 (E10) indicates this growth is not fully priced in. Multiple direct, current data points agree, supporting high confidence.

Margins are exceptional across the board: 74.1% gross, 65.6% operating, and 63.0% net (E13, E14, E15), with return on equity of 114.3% (E16). These are direct, current, and mutually consistent figures indicating elite operating leverage and capital efficiency.

The company holds $53.17B in cash against only $12.81B of total debt (E19, E20), a net-cash position of roughly $40B, and a current ratio of 3.44 indicates ample short-term liquidity (E22). The reported debt/equity figure of 6.55 (E21) is immaterial given cash comfortably exceeds debt. Financial health is strong with high confidence.

Relative to growth the valuation is attractive: forward P/E of 16.30 and PEG of 0.63 (E8, E10), and the $298.93 analyst mean target implies ~44% upside from the $207.41 price (E3, E2). Against this, trailing P/E of 31.81 is moderate-to-elevated and price/book of 25.70 is very rich (E7, E9). Confidence is medium because the signals are mixed (asset multiples rich, growth-adjusted multiples cheap) and valuation is inherently forward-looking.

Operating cash flow of $125.65B TTM and free cash flow of $46.34B TTM (E18, E17) are both strongly positive and large in absolute terms. The gap between OCF and FCF implies heavy capital expenditure/investment intensity, but cash generation remains robustly positive, supporting a strong rating.

The evidence contains only a qualitative business description of NVIDIA as a data-center-scale AI infrastructure company operating through Compute & Networking and Graphics segments (E29). No competitive metrics are provided — no market share, pricing power, customer concentration, switching costs, or peer comparison — so a moat judgment cannot be grounded in evidence and is marked insufficient_data.

Sentiment is strongly favorable: a strong_buy consensus from 59 analysts (E26, E27), a 52-week price gain of 47.4% (E25), and a mean target of $298.93 well above the $207.41 price (E3, E2). The price sits about 12% below the 52-week high of $236.54 and well above the $142.03 low (E4, E5). A beta of 2.20 (E24) signals high volatility, which tempers but does not negate the positive momentum.

Concrete risk signals are present: price/book of 25.70 and trailing P/E of 31.81 represent stretched valuation multiples (E9, E7), and a beta of 2.20 indicates amplified drawdown risk in a downturn (E24); the price is also ~12% below its 52-week high of $236.54 (E2, E4). These are partially offset by low leverage and strong cash flow, so confidence is medium. The recent news headlines (E30–E34) are off-topic and were excluded as non-evidence per the risk-rating rules.

key_risks: Stretched asset-based valuation: price/book of 25.70 and trailing P/E of 31.81 (E9, E7) leave little margin for execution missteps.
High volatility: beta of 2.20 (E24) implies roughly double the market's drawdown sensitivity.
Capital intensity: free cash flow of $46.34B is far below operating cash flow of $125.65B (E17, E18), reflecting heavy capex that could pressure returns if growth slows.
Price is ~12% below its 52-week high of $236.54 (E2, E4), indicating recent drawdown from peak.
data_gaps: No competitive, market-share, pricing-power, or customer-concentration data — competitive position / moat cannot be assessed.
No historical margin or cash-flow trend; only current-period snapshots are provided (limits durability assessment).
No share count, dilution, or buyback data to evaluate per-share growth or capital-return policy beyond the 0.47% dividend yield.
No segment-level or geographic revenue breakdown despite a multi-segment, multi-region business (E29).
No forward guidance, backlog, or management commentary.
